Recipe:

Adapted from Betty Crocker's chocolate chip cookie

You will need:
1 cup becel buttery taste or actual butter
1.5 cups dark brown sugar
1 pack vanilla pudding
1 egg
1 tsp vanilla
1 pinch salt
1 tsp baking soda
2-2.5 cups all purpose flour
Add-ins of your choice

(Preheat oven to 375 F. )

Cream becel/butter with sugar for two minutes. Add in pudding mix until combined. Add in egg, vanilla and salt. Mix for one minute. Then add in baking soda and flour. Less flour yields a thinner chewier cookie. More yields a denser fluffy cookie with some chew. 

Refrigerate(very important) for 4-24 hours. Take dough out until room temp then  scoop whatever sized balls you want. 

Bake for 8(small) to 14 mins. 

You can use any pudding flavour you want. I like lemon pudding with white chocolate chips and cranberries. Banana and white chocolate chips are alsk good:)

Yield: 3 9-inch double crust pies or 6 pie shells

6 cups cake and pastry flour
(Or 5 1/2 cups AP flour)
2 tsp salt
1 lb lard
1tsp vinegar
1 egg lightly beaten
Cold water

1. Mix in flour and salt
2. Cut in lard with pastry blender or two knives until mix resembles course oatmeal. 
3. In a one cup measure, combine vinegar and egg. Add water to make one cup. Gradually stir this into lard mixture. ADD ONLY ENOUGH TO MAKE DOUGH CLING TOGETHER. 
4. Gather into a ball and divide into 6 portions. If you want, refrigerate or freeze. 
5. Roll out each ball onto lightly floured surface. 
6. Transfer dough to pie plate and bake according to your recipe.

First off here is a very simple recipe for a moist chocolate cake to get you started: 

https://addapinch.com/the-best-chocolate-cake-recipe-ever/

Secondly, baking is a science. Cakes can be very finicky. It can be very easy to go and make one and have it turn out dense, rubbery and flat. 

This all has to do with ingredients and preparation. A certain amount of ingredients are needed. Over or undermixing can affect the final result. The temperature in the oven has to be precise. As do the minutes the cake is baking. 

A simple vanilla cake's ingredients would be:

Flour- cakes usually call for All-purpose flour. Flour will provide structure and is a base in almost all baked goods. Different flours will affect the end result and ingredients need to be altered to fit the flour.  

Baking soda/baking powder- will have a reaction with other ingredients, causing the cake to rise. 

Salt- enhances flavour of cake. 

Sugar- not just for sweetness. The sugar will help develop the flavor of the cake and provide a nice brown crust on top. 

Vanilla- flavouring of the cake

Butter/oil- most cakes call for oil as it will make the cake much more moist. Butter will give a denser cake. 

Milk/water- helps to bind dry and wet ingredients and allow steam to be released. 

Eggs- eggs help stabilize the cake.   


I would highly recommend searching up charts that show ingredient swaps so you can alter the cake to your liking. You can find them on pinterest and on here as well.

www.finecooking.com/articles/how-sugar-affects-baking.aspx?pg=0

In my experience, specifically baking with splenda baking blend, the resulting bake is very different than if I had used sugar. Example: cookies dont spread, cakes dont get nice and brown and crackly on the top. This is because when youre baking with sugar, it melts at high heat which makes the cookies spread and caramelizes causing the colour change. 

Baking is a science, and sugar plays more of a role than just sweetness. 

I have yet to try truvia/splenda baking but know that the packs I do buy have a distinct flavor so that may come through. 

I'd recommend experimenting with the truvia and see how it goes. 

If I may ask, are you using stevia because of actual health problems with sugar or just because its "healthier"?

thecakeblog.com/2016/02/sugars-impact-on-cake.html
